title: risc
summary: This is a satirical, humorous text in the form of an internal computer-industry newsletter or mailing-list digest, parodying the terse, jargon-heavy style of technical reference documentation and bulletin-board exchanges from the Honeywell GCOS8/DPS8 mainframe era. It opens with a supposed erratum to the reference manual, playfully reinterpreting the abbreviation MBZ ("must be zero") as "might be zero," "could be zero," or "transfer on maybe." It then presents a list of invented assembler instructions and operators with absurd functions: a "load virtually everytime" instruction, a "test litmus paper" instruction, a "test rabbit" instruction that skips the program if the rabbit is deceased, and an assembly-time operator for neither/nor logic. Further sections mock government procurement requirements, bureaucratic development schedules, and staff meetings. The author is not named in the excerpt, and the piece is a lighthearted send-up of programming culture rather than a real technical document.
